takeshima.question_template: Should record {label} be retained for a review of light therapy for bipolar disorder?
takeshima.criteria:
Screen the supplied title and abstract only; do not require full text.

Eligibility: Individual- or cluster-randomized controlled trials; crossover trials require available first-period results before crossover. Participants have clinical bipolar I or II disorder diagnosed using any recognized criteria, in any mood state, including depression, mania, or euthymia. At least 80% of participants must have bipolar I/II disorder. The intervention is any light therapy, including bright light therapy, phototherapy, or chronotherapy involving light, at any intensity or color. Controls receive sham treatment (including low-intensity light, dim red light, or negative ions) or treatment as usual without light treatment. Any language is eligible. No age, dose, timing, duration, background-medication, or specific-outcome restriction is added.

Retain eligible or plausibly relevant records when eligibility is uncertain or details are unreported. Missing evidence is not a demonstrated violation: unclear randomization, diagnosis, bipolar proportion, light component, control, or first-period data does not justify exclusion. Do not infer that unspecified depression is unipolar. Missing outcomes or nonsignificant findings are not exclusions.

Exclude plainly unrelated records or demonstrated incompatibilities in design, population, intervention, or comparator, including explicitly nonrandomized studies, nonhuman research, reviews, below-80% bipolar samples, non-light interventions, or absence of an eligible comparison. Explicitly unavailable first-period results differ from unreported details. Assess the underlying trial: secondary reports and multiarm trials may qualify through an eligible comparison.

maruki.question_template: Should record {label} be retained for a review of adjunctive second-generation antipsychotic or mood-stabilizer therapy for bipolar depression?
maruki.criteria:
Screen the supplied title and abstract only; do not require full text.

Eligibility: Individual- or cluster-randomized controlled trials; crossover trials require available first-phase results before crossover. Participants have bipolar I or II depression diagnosed using any recognized criteria; mixed features and rapid cycling are allowed. Participants are not taking antidepressants during the evaluated treatment. Eligible mood stabilizers (MS) are carbamazepine, lithium, lamotrigine, and valproic acid (including valproate/divalproex). Add a second-generation antipsychotic (SGA) or eligible MS to baseline SGA/MS treatment, compared with adjunctive placebo during baseline SGA/MS treatment. Follow these Methods criteria, not the narrower drug list in the title. Outcome assessment is described at baseline and endpoints before 12 weeks; longer follow-up alone does not establish absence of eligible short-term assessment.

Retain eligible or plausibly relevant records when eligibility is uncertain or details are unreported. Missing evidence is not a demonstrated violation, including unclear randomization, diagnosis, antidepressant use, background therapy, comparator, first-phase data, or assessment timing. Prior antidepressant use is not current co-treatment. Missing outcomes or nonsignificant findings are not exclusions.

Exclude plainly unrelated records or demonstrated design, population, intervention, or comparator incompatibilities: explicitly nonrandomized studies, nonhuman research, reviews, nondepressive populations, current antidepressant co-treatment, ineligible drugs, or no placebo-adjunct comparison. Explicitly unavailable first-phase data differ from unreported details. Secondary reports and multiarm trials may qualify through an eligible comparison. Add no adult-only, treatment-resistance, language, sample-size, dose, or 80%-bipolar requirements.
